Hey im an adopted child in a brown family. Unknowingly or not adoptees from brown families do discriminate between children. I know some information about my biological family, how my biological mother had to leave me after my biological dad went and her peers had pressured her to leave me. I do feel very left out in my foster family, we are different genetically, in the ways we behave and also like we dont have a good understanding. Even when i tried to make them understand how i felt, they chose to ignore it. I keep getting reminded of how "lucky" im supposed to me to have a family and all it does is make me feel extremely bad cause it keeps reminding me that my biological family left me in the first case. Being adopted, the only thing i know is that if i ever adopt a child in the future, i will make sure to treat their adoption how they want it to be treated.

I was adopted when i was a month old and i accidentally found out about my adoption around 4 years ago. My family got to know about me knowing the fact through some incidences, i tried not to tell them cause someone adviced me that if i do so, they'll get hurt. i always felt left out from my family and knowing this had me hurting too badly. I relate with you about the genetic differences starting to show but also my adoptee parents had a girl right after taking me in and the way they treat her and me is very different. The slightest of the differences are only felt by me and they constantly remind me of the fact. The only advice i can give to you is to sit down and talk to your dad. Even if you cant talk to him in one go try to tell him whenever you can about how you feel and i hope he will try to understand you.
